title: Evidence payload
description: The evidence block a subagent returns for one company. Enforces P2 (only evidence a stranger could inspect without asking) and P5 (when a record is missing, name the missing record). Structural keywords here are checked by src/utils/schemaValidator.js; the two cross-cutting rules that JSON Schema cannot express are listed in x-rules and implemented in the same file.

dated.description: The date the evidence was gathered. Every generated artifact carries a date.

acquittal.description: INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE is an acquittal, not a finding of innocence. A company can have a bottleneck that cannot be established through admissible process. Saying so is a finding under P5, and requires missing_record.

missing_record.description: Required when acquittal is INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE. The name of the record that would settle the question. P5.

evidence.description: One row per claim. May be empty only under an INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE acquittal.

claim.description: One assertion. Not a summary of several.

inspectable_at.description: An absolute URL a stranger can open without contacting anyone. A bare repo path is not inspectable by a stranger, so repo evidence must be written as a full blob or commit URL.

verify_seconds.description: How long verification takes, in whole seconds. The auditor passes anything verifiable in ten seconds; filing-standard question 10 vetoes anything over sixty. The threshold is the auditor's judgment, not this schema's, so only the measurement is required here. src/utils/latencyGuard.js measures the fetch time to inspectable_at and can prove this number impossible, never prove it right: a fetch is a floor, and reading the page is the part that takes the time.

pramana_class.description: How this row is known, not how strongly. Indian epistemology separates the means of knowledge from the confidence in it, and this repository had only the second: strength 1-5 says how sure, and nothing said how. DIRECT_OBSERVABLE is a thing a stranger reads off a machine — a commit, raw API JSON, a status-page outage. TESTIMONY is someone's account of themselves: marketing copy, a press release, the posting's own description. INFERRED_RELATION is a conclusion drawn from an observable through a stated invariant, and requires vyapti. HYPOTHETICAL is a suspicion carried for the record and cannot support anything. Optional on artifacts dated before the cutover in src/utils/schemaValidator.js, where the class is derived from source_class and reported as derived.

expected_status.description: The HTTP status this citation is expected to return, when that is not 200. Set it when the ABSENCE is the finding: a claim that a repository publishes no .github directory is proved by a 404 at that path, and src/utils/latencyGuard.js would otherwise report the citation as dead. Declaring it converts a negative observation from a broken link into a checkable one. Do not use it to excuse a citation that rotted.

vyapti.description: Required on INFERRED_RELATION. The invariant that licenses the inference, written out: the 'wherever smoke, there fire' of this particular claim. Naming it is what makes an inference checkable, because a stranger can then attack the invariant instead of the conclusion. An inference whose pervasion nobody wrote down is an assertion with a longer sentence in front of it.

source_class.description: Frontstage is what the company manages to appear to be: the posting, the marketing site, the careers page. Backstage traces are involuntary: pull request age, issue age weighted by demand, release gaps, refusal clustering.

strength.description: 5 a sovereign backstage trace a stranger can reproduce; 3 circumstantial, consistent with the claim but also with others; 1 asserted with a source that only repeats the assertion.

specificity_leak.description: Marks a frontstage row that is admissible anyway because it is where frontstage control failed: a detail too specific to be presentation. Must be labeled, per .claude/agents/diagnostician.md. This is the one exception to R-BACKSTAGE.

query_issued.description: The query issued to kill the hypothesis, formed after the hypothesis. Scored on disconfirming evidence sought, not found.

result.description: What came back, including the word nothing. A logged query with no logged result is not a logged attempt.

survived.description: Whether the hypothesis survived the query.

x-rules.description: A payload claiming EVIDENCE_SUFFICIENT must carry at least one backstage row, or one frontstage row explicitly labeled specificity_leak. An evidence set that is entirely frontstage is the company's own account of itself and cannot establish a constraint. NARROWED 2026-08-17 by R-PRAMANA-INTEGRITY: the labeled-leak escape still satisfies this rule, but a set consisting only of leaks now fails the DIRECT_OBSERVABLE floor. A leak is still the company talking, and it is admissible as corroboration rather than as the sole basis of a sufficiency claim.

An EVIDENCE_SUFFICIENT payload needs at least one DIRECT_OBSERVABLE. TESTIMONY is admissible only on a row flagged specificity_leak, which is the same exception R-BACKSTAGE already carves for frontstage: a company's account of itself becomes evidence exactly where its control of the account failed. INFERRED_RELATION requires vyapti naming the invariant. HYPOTHETICAL supports nothing and is carried for the record only.
EVIDENCE_SUFFICIENT requires at least one evidence row. INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE requires missing_record naming the record that would settle it. P5.
